domain: team dinner at a Korean BBQ restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

Derek was diagnosed with celiac disease last year

Priya wants to bring her roommate Nina, so that makes five

ground_truth.answer: Haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) is problematic for Sam — his allergy was upgraded from shellfish to all seafood, and a seafood pancake directly contains seafood. Salmon sashimi has two problems: Sam cannot eat it (seafood allergy) and Nina should avoid it (pregnant, raw fish). Bulgogi (marinated beef) needs to be confirmed as using gluten-free soy sauce for Derek (celiac disease) — if the restaurant uses their dedicated gluten-free soy sauce for the marinade, it's fine; otherwise it's a problem. Galbi (short ribs in soy marinade) has the same gluten concern for Derek — needs gluten-free soy sauce. Japchae (glass noodles with vegetables) is fine for everyone — glass noodles are made from sweet potato starch, not wheat. Tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes) is fine for everyone currently attending — rice cakes are gluten-free, and Priya (the Jain diner) is no longer coming.
required_elements: Haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) is problematic for Sam because his allergy was upgraded to all seafood, not just shellfish
Salmon sashimi is problematic for Sam because of his all-seafood allergy
Salmon sashimi is problematic for Nina because she is pregnant and should avoid raw fish
Bulgogi needs to use gluten-free soy sauce in the marinade for Derek due to his celiac disease
Galbi needs to use gluten-free soy sauce in the marinade for Derek due to his celiac disease
Japchae is fine for everyone currently attending
Tteokbokki is fine for everyone currently attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging any dish as problematic for Priya or citing Jain dietary restrictions (Priya is no longer attending)
Saying Sam only has a shellfish allergy (it was upgraded to all seafood including oyster-based sauces)
Flagging tteokbokki as containing gluten (rice cakes are gluten-free)
Saying salmon sashimi is fine for Sam (he has an all-seafood allergy, not just shellfish)
Saying salmon sashimi is fine for Nina without noting the raw fish concern for pregnancy
Flagging bulgogi or galbi as completely off-limits for Derek without mentioning the gluten-free soy sauce option the restaurant offers
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint upgrade reasoning across 10 conversational turns. The primary difficulty mechanism is the constraint UPGRADE: Sam's allergy starts as shellfish-only (shrimp hives incident) and is later corrected to all seafood including oyster-based sauces. The agent must apply the UPGRADED constraint at probe time, not the original. Additional tracking challenges: (1) Derek has celiac disease (inferential: celiac → no gluten), but the restaurant offers gluten-free soy sauce — so soy-marinated dishes are conditionally OK, not automatically rejected. (2) Nina joins late (Turn 3) with an inferential constraint (pregnant → no raw fish), which makes salmon sashimi problematic for her. (3) Priya EXITS (Turn 6) — her Jain dietary constraint should be completely removed. Nina, who Priya brought, STAYS — so Nina's pregnancy constraint persists even though her connection to the group (Priya) left. (4) The over-generalization trap: Sam's original shellfish allergy might cause the agent to only flag shellfish items, missing that salmon sashimi is also seafood and now problematic after the upgrade. (5) Tteokbokki tests false-positive suppression — rice cakes are gluten-free, so Derek is fine with them, and Priya's Jain restriction no longer applies.

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
